fixes.explanation: Mouths feel like a fair guess, since this is a whole passage about speaking. But the LORD names something different: "…with the works of your hands." (Jeremiah 25:7). He says that is what provoked Him to anger. So hands, not mouths, are in this verse.

I wish that were the answer, friend. But Jeremiah says the opposite: "…I have spoken to you again and again, but you have not listened." (Jeremiah 25:3). The word kept coming, and the people kept walking right past it.

Elders are a fair guess, but they're not who this verse names. It says, "…the LORD has sent all His servants the prophets to you again and again…" (Jeremiah 25:4). The prophets were the ones carrying the LORD's word. Jeremiah was one of them, so he had company on this long road.
Yes! The prophets said, "Do not follow other gods to serve and worship them…" (Jeremiah 25:6). That was the second warning sitting right beside turning from evil ways. It's a clear one.

Egypt is a fair guess, but that warning isn't in this verse. Here the prophets say, "Do not follow other gods to serve and worship them…" (Jeremiah 25:6). That's the warning that went with turning from evil ways.

Right on. The LORD says, "…I will send for My servant Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon…" (Jeremiah 25:9). Remember, the LORD says this is because Judah has not obeyed His words. I wouldn't have seen that name coming.
Pharaoh Neco is a reasonable guess, but he isn't the name here. The LORD says, "…I will send for My servant Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon…" (Jeremiah 25:9). Babylon, not Egypt, is the answer.
Cyrus is a fair guess, but his name isn't in this verse. Here the LORD says, "…I will send for My servant Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon…" (Jeremiah 25:9). That's Babylon's king, not Persia's.

Yes. The LORD says He will bring Nebuchadnezzar "…against this land, against its residents, and against all the surrounding nations." (Jeremiah 25:9). So it's Judah and the nations around it. The surrounding nations are named right there with Judah.

Sheba is a fair guess, but it isn't named in this verse. The LORD says He will bring Nebuchadnezzar "…against this land, against its residents, and against all the surrounding nations." (Jeremiah 25:9). That means Judah and its neighbors. This one stays close to home.

Marching armies make sense with all this talk of Babylon, but they aren't on the list. The LORD says He will banish "…the sounds of joy and gladness, the voices of the bride and bridegroom, the sound of the millstones, and the light of the lamp." (Jeremiah 25:10). Those are the sounds and lights of ordinary, happy life. I think this one hurts.

That's right. The LORD says, "…when seventy years are complete, I will punish the king of Babylon and that nation, the land of the Chaldeans, for their guilt…" (Jeremiah 25:12). Nebuchadnezzar was called His servant in verse 9, and the king of Babylon and his nation still answer for their guilt. The seventy years have an end.

It's actually true, friend. The LORD says of the Chaldeans' land, "…I will make it an everlasting desolation." (Jeremiah 25:12). It sounds like a big turn after Nebuchadnezzar is called His servant in verse 9, but the verse says it plainly.
